newsitem.title: UK: London gold in tight range after recent losses.
newsitem.headline: London gold in tight range after recent losses.

text.p: Precious metals consolidated in narrow price bands on Monday after being hit by sharp falls last week, dealers said.
Gold fixed little changed at $378.70 an ounce, versus $378.65 in the morning.
Gold had sunk some $5.00 an ounce last week on selling linked to gold miners, a central bank and speculators. A fresh test of recent lows just under $377 was possible, dealers said.
But some said that with most of the market expecting prices to head lower, an upturn seemed more likely. Prices had ticked up more than $1.00 since Friday's London close.

"It seems a bit of a bear trap, we may have seen the low for the moment," one said. "We may see a bit of consolidation, a bit of buying now," he added, pegging the near term maximum at the important $380.00 level.
Analysts said South Africa's gold output this year would fail to reach the 500 tonnes previously forecast, which might be construed by the market as bullish.
Price charts showed gold at $376.80 and $376.90 recently. Analysts said this suggested a "double bottom" formation had emerged, providing support for gold at that level.
But both the 10- and 30-day moving averages were moving lower, which indicated gold's downward movement had accelerated.
Dealers said a recent surge in the cost of borrowing gold was still causing some anxiety in the market.
Towards the year-end the market tends to tighten as central banks cut back lending in order to audit their reserves.
But bearish expectations that central banks planned to sell some of their gold reserves and that gold miners intended to sell more metal were also seen behind the tightening.
Producers typically sell gold which they have not yet mined by borrowing metal from central banks to sell. They pay the bank back once their own gold has been mined and refined.
The market may pick up following the U.S. presidential election on Tuesday, dealers said.
"We may some more life after the (U.S. presidential) elections, although what Clinton has to do with gold is a mystery," one dealer said.
Silver was firmer with gold, up four cents from Friday's London close at $4.81/$4.83. Platinum was up $1.50 at $381.00/$382.00, and palladium was up $0.25 at $116.00/$117.00.
"Silver and platinum have been holding quite well, and they are going to be key," a dealer said.
